graders.name: answer
graders.evidence:
The feature list is confirmed from the official docs. I could not find out whether people are hitting bugs.

**What it supports**

The source is the official Valkey docs page for valkey-search 1.2 on Valkey 9 (valkey.io/topics/search, updated 2026-10-01).

- **Supported:**
  - Vector similarity search with HNSW and FLAT indexes.
  - Numeric filters.
  - Tag filters.
  - Hybrid queries that combine vector search with numeric and tag filters.
- **Not supported:** full-text search. The docs say it is planned for a future release and give no date.

So today it works as a vector and filter engine, not a general search engine. If you need text relevance or BM25-style ranking, it can't do that yet.

**Bugs**

I have no evidence either way.
- The GitHub issue searches returned nothing.
- Scrapes of the valkey-search issues page and repo root failed.
- The `last30days` skill isn't installed, so I didn't search practitioner and social discussion.

Don't read this as "no bugs." Before relying on it, check the open issues at github.com/valkey-io/valkey-search directly, or tell me to retry with a different fetch route.

I saved the docs excerpt and a wiki page, "Valkey Search", to the vault. The page records the bug question as unknown, and lint came back clean.

**Coverage:**
- Docs: Exa, Tavily and Firecrawl all gave the same page.
- GitHub issues: Tavily returned nothing, and Firecrawl failed on the issues page and repo root.
- Social: `last30days` not installed.
- Paid spend: none.

graders.name: answer
graders.evidence:
**Short answer:** Drizzle v1 is usable in production, but review every generated migration before you apply it. I'd upgrade to 1.0.3 or later. The evidence that it's ready is thin: one team's post, and I only got its headline.

v1.0 shipped 2026-09-15. Version 1.0.3 came out 2026-10-29.

**Breaking changes from 0.x** (from the [official upgrade guide](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/upgrade-v1)):
- **Relational queries v2 is now the default.** Check any code that uses relational queries.
- **`drizzle-kit push` is now `drizzle-kit sync`.** Update your scripts and CI.
- **PostgreSQL drivers must be node-postgres 9+ or postgres.js 4+.**

The page text I retrieved listed only these three and said a migration guide is on the page. I didn't see the guide's steps, so read it in full. There may be other breaks I haven't seen.

**Known issues:**
- **Open data-loss risk ([#5120](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/5120)).** When you change an enum, v1 generates a migration that drops and recreates the column. Hand-edit the generated migration before you apply it. The issue has 61 comments and is still open.
- **Fixed in 1.0.3 ([#5188](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/5188)).** Relational queries v2 returned the wrong nesting for self-relations. Don't go live on anything older than 1.0.3.

**Practitioner report:** [One team ran v1 in production for a month](https://blog.example-dev.io/drizzle-v1-in-production) (2026-10-18) and said it was "solid, but review every generated migration." I only got the headline, and it's a single source.

**Before you upgrade:**
1. Pin 1.0.3 or later and try it on a staging copy of your database.
2. Diff every generated migration, especially ones that touch enums.
3. Rerun your tests for relational queries, especially self-relations.
4. Change `push` to `sync` in your scripts.
5. Check your Postgres driver version.

I don't know about MySQL or SQLite adapter issues, or any other Drizzle Kit changes beyond the rename. Tell me which database and driver you use and I can look into those.

I saved the findings to the vault at `wiki/Drizzle ORM v1.md`, with the four sources, an index entry and a log line. Lint passed with no errors.

**Coverage:**
- **Vault:** nothing on Drizzle existed beforehand.
- **Exa:** found the upgrade guide and issues, and I fetched the guide and #5120 in full.
- **Tavily:** gave the same results, with dates.
- **Firecrawl:** not used.
- **Social lane:** `last30days` isn't installed, so I didn't search social sources.

Spend was about $0.002.

graders.name: answer
graders.evidence:
**Drizzle v1 is usable in production if you're careful. Pin to 1.0.3 or later, and read every generated migration before you apply it.**

v1.0 shipped on 2026-09-15.

**Breaking changes from 0.x**, per the [official upgrade guide](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/upgrade-v1):
- **Relational queries v2 is now the default.** Check any code that uses `db.query`.
- **`drizzle-kit push` is now `drizzle-kit sync`.** Update your scripts and CI.
- **Postgres drivers have minimum versions.** You need node-postgres 9+ or postgres.js 4+.

**Known problems:**
- **Open, data-loss risk:** an enum change generates a migration that drops and recreates the column ([#5120](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/5120), opened 2026-10-03, 61 comments). The workaround is to hand-edit the migration before applying it. If you edit enums, this is the main blocker.
- **Fixed in 1.0.3 (2026-10-29):** relational queries v2 returned wrong nesting for tables with self-relations ([#5188](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/5188)).

**Practitioner evidence is thin.** One [blog post](https://blog.example-dev.io/drizzle-v1-in-production) reports a month in production and calls it "solid, but review every generated migration." It's a single source with no detail.

**What I couldn't confirm:**
- The guide I retrieved only summarised the three breaking changes, so there may be more.
- I don't know whether #5120 has been fixed since 1.0.3.
- I only checked Postgres. MySQL and SQLite weren't covered.

Before upgrading, read the full migration guide and check #5120's status. Then run a sync or generate against a copy of your database and diff the SQL.

I saved the findings and sources to the vault as `wiki/Drizzle ORM v1.md`.

**Coverage:**
- **Vault:** no prior page on this topic.
- **Docs:** Exa gave the upgrade guide.
- **Issues:** Exa and Tavily both returned the two GitHub issues.
- **Practitioner reports:** one blog post.
- **Social:** `last30days` wasn't used, so that lane is missing.
- **Cost:** no paid spend.
